text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The value of turnover on the Egyptian stock exchange has been 6.2 billion pounds so far this year and Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the sudden jump in turnover showed full confidence in the Egyptian economic environment and that Egypt has become one of the countries in the region best qualified to attract Arab, foreign and Egyptian investment.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi welcomed the Ethiopian death sentences against the three Egyptians convicted of trying to kill Mubarak and said they showed that Sudan was involved in the assassination plot.

- In New York Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said there was clear support for gving U.S. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali a second term in office, including support from the Organisation of African Unity and the Arab League.

- An official source in the cabinet confirmed that the former chairman of the Holding Company for Engineering Industries, Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, and his children were banned from travel on June 20 pending a judicial inquiry. It did not say why.

- Mubarak has sent letters to the Emir of Kuwait, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, the Emir of Bahrain, Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi. The letters are about supporting the peace process and the report submitted to Mubarak by the Arab foreign ministers.
- Moussa said that peace was foundering on the rock of Israeli rejection because of intransigence on the question of Jewish settlements.

- The state security prosecutor has started questioning members of a new terrorist organisation which includes 16 members of a group which calls itself the military wing of Jihad. The group is led by Raafat al-Tunsi Abdelhamid.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the state would spare no effort to promote all aspects of education. He said that since 1990 the state has built 6,000 schools, more than it had done in the previous 108 years.
- The water level in Lake Nasser rose another nine cm (three and a half inches) yesterday to reach 177.31 metres.
- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi opened the extension at the lubricating oil plant at Meks in Alexandria and said it was the first time the private sector had joined petroleum projects.
- Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi said revenue from tourism in 1995/6 was $3,009.1 million, an increase of $710.2 million or 30.9 percent over the previous year.
